title: Live Animal Export Prohibition (Ending Cruelty) Bill 2014
short_title: Live Animal Export Prohibition (Ending Cruelty) Bill 2014

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would phase out exports of live livestock for slaughter and impose a complete ban on that trade from 1 July 2017.
Before the ban, exports would generally require the Secretary to be satisfied about animal treatment, including holding conditions, transport, handling and slaughter standards.
The legislation would start on Royal Assent, with limited temporary exemptions for some export contracts made before commencement and no exemptions from the final ban.
changes: Licence holders would have to make reasonable efforts to ensure compliance with international animal treatment guidelines.
Licence holders learning of breaches would have to notify the Secretary within 14 days.
The normal treatment test would require stunning immediately before slaughter.
Contract exemptions for exports three to six months after commencement would require reasonable renegotiation and welfare efforts.
summary.affected: Livestock export licence holders and people proposing live livestock exports for slaughter are affected.
